steps.tx: **Dermatomyositis** is an inflammatory myopathy with a pathognomonic rash of heliotrope discoloration and Gottron papules. Proximal symmetric weakness with dysphagia is the motor presentation. **Elevated creatine kinase** is typical and **perifascicular atrophy** on biopsy is diagnostic. **Interstitial lung disease** is the major complication and needs screening.

steps.tx: **Complement attack** on endomysial capillaries starts dermatomyositis, causing capillary loss with watershed ischaemia and **perifascicular atrophy** in about 50% of patients. Polymyositis is direct **CD8 T cell** invasion of non necrotic fibres expressing MHC class 1. **Interferon driven** inflammation links the skin and muscle injury. Inclusion body disease adds rimmed vacuoles with degeneration that resists immunotherapy.

steps.tx: **Polymyositis** is proximal weakness without rash, and **muscle biopsy** shows endomysial CD8 infiltrates invading non necrotic fibres. **Inclusion body myositis** affects the elderly with finger flexor and quadriceps weakness and dysphagia. **Immune mediated necrotising myopathy** follows statin exposure in many patients. Each has a different biopsy pattern and prognosis.

steps.tx: **Myositis specific antibodies** define the subsets: **anti Mi2** with dermatomyositis, **anti Jo1** with interstitial lung disease, and **anti SRP** with necrotising myopathy. **Anti HMGCR** follows statin exposure in necrotising disease. **Anti MDA5** causes rapidly progressive lung disease. Antibody testing is part of the baseline evaluation.

steps.tx: **Creatine kinase** is markedly raised and is the first test. **Magnetic resonance imaging** of thigh shows muscle oedema and fatty replacement. **Muscle biopsy** is definitive and is taken from an affected non necrotic muscle. **Pulmonary function tests** and high resolution computed tomography screen the lungs. The **antibody panel** is part of the baseline workup.

steps.tx: **High dose corticosteroids** are first line and **methotrexate** and **azathioprine** are common steroid sparing drugs. **Intravenous immunoglobulin** helps dermatomyositis with skin and swallowing involvement. **Inclusion body myositis** does not respond to immunosuppression. **Physiotherapy** starts with therapy and continues through recovery.

steps.tx: **Malignancy** is strongly linked to dermatomyositis, especially in older patients and those with anti TIF1 and anti NXP2 antibodies. **Age appropriate cancer screening** is mandatory at diagnosis. **Interstitial lung disease** needs pulmonology co care and early immunosuppression. **Dysphagia** with aspiration needs swallowing assessment.

steps.tx: **Rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease** with anti MDA5 antibodies can kill within months and needs early **rituximab**. **Dysphagia** causes aspiration pneumonia, **myocarditis** causes arrhythmia, and calcinosis complicates juvenile disease. Overall **5 year survival is 70 to 93%**, worse with older age, lung disease, cardiac involvement, or cancer. Organ involvement decides treatment intensity and follow up.

steps.tx: **Traps** test biopsy patterns and nonresponse. Perifascicular atrophy is dermatomyositis, rimmed vacuoles are inclusion body myositis, and necrosis predominates in necrotising disease. **Inclusion body myositis** has no response to immunosuppression. **Statin exposure** points to anti HMGCR necrotising disease. Malignancy screening is mandatory in dermatomyositis.

Anti Jo1 brings lung disease and malignancy screening is mandatory in dermatomyositis.
